qc.label_under_test: The opening piece of a strong verdict (good or bad) that is still unfinished, in a judging slot after is/was/a: it lights up on the first piece of a split or hyphenated verdict word or set phrase, already before the rest arrives (was truly ground-breaking, was mind-blowing, was jaw-dropping, was out of this world, a first-class job, INC-REDIBLE / HORRIBLE in ALL CAPS, German war außergewöhnlich, French était hors norme, Russian зам-ечательный). Quiet on the same opening words in literal uses (turned the ground over, a ground-floor shed, walked out of the room, changed her mind, broke his jaw), on strong verdicts written as one ordinary token (incredible, extraordinary, wonderful), on finished intensifiers (absolutely, extremely), and on mild verdicts (okay, fine, gut). Exception: German außerhalb ('outside') also fires on its opening piece.

neighbours.label: The opening piece of a strong verdict (good or bad) that is split into several tokens, lighting up on that first piece before the rest arrives: hyphenated verdict compounds (ground-breaking, mind-blowing, jaw-dropping, mouth-watering, world-class, first-class, state-of-the-art), verdict set phrases (out of this world, second to none), strong verdicts written in ALL CAPS (FANTASTIC, INCREDIBLE, HORRIBLE), and foreign strong verdicts that split (German unglaublich, außergewöhnlich; French hors norme; Russian замечательный). Strongest right after is/was/a, and also fires before a noun (a mouth-watering roast). Quiet on the same opening words used literally (broke his jaw, a hair-band, the ground floor), on neutral or mild hyphenated words (hand-made, water-proof, well-written, ill-conceived, over-priced, so-so), and on strong verdicts written as one ordinary lowercase token (fantastic, incredible, wonderful). Bare 'state' and 'ground' in non-verdict uses can fire weakly.
fire: The new vaccine research was ground-breaking, according to every reviewer.
Honestly, the final scene of that film was mind-blowing.
She served a mouth-watering roast with garlic potatoes for the holiday dinner.
The view from the summit was jaw-dropping at sunrise.
The hotel offers world-class service and a spa on every floor.
Their lab uses state-of-the-art equipment for every test.
Grandma's apple pie is out of this world.
When it comes to customer care, this little shop is second to none.
quiet: The workers broke ground on the new library last Tuesday.
Honestly, the final scene of that film was well-written.
She served a hand-made pie with garlic potatoes for the holiday dinner.
The boxer broke his jaw in the third round.
The hotel offers water-proof jackets and a spa on every floor.
Their lab is on the ground floor of the old building.
Grandma's apple pie is a little over-priced at the market.
When it comes to customer care, this little shop is so-so.

predictions: Loop-back refine after mapping neighbours (break, cass, supply, error-message cells: none changes the meaning). Expect most fire items to clear 0.2; the risk is the two 'ground' near misses, which the label flags as weak.
